title: Postgres
description: PostgreSQL servers in config/postgres.toml, probed from the monitoring VM every minute.

panels.title: Up
panels.description: Probed from the monitoring VM every minute. VM: the VM answers on TCP (SSH port). PostgreSQL port: a TCP connection to PostgreSQL succeeds from the network. Metrics endpoint: the server's pg-monitor answers. PostgreSQL: pg-monitor could query the database (only known while the endpoint answers).

panels.title: PostgreSQL port reachable, selected range
panels.description: Share of probes over the selected time range in which PostgreSQL's port accepted a TCP connection from the monitoring VM.

panels.title: Data disk free
panels.description: Free space on the partition holding the database (/data). It also holds WAL that is waiting to be archived, which grows if backups to shire fail.

panels.title: Last backup
panels.description: Time since the most recent successful backup of any type finished. Backups run nightly.

panels.title: Last full backup
panels.description: Time since the most recent successful full backup finished. Fulls run weekly.

panels.title: Last backup job
panels.description: Whether the scheduler's most recent backup run succeeded.

panels.title: WAL archiving
panels.description: Failing if PostgreSQL's most recent attempt to copy WAL to the backup repository failed. WAL archiving is what makes point-in-time recovery possible; while it fails, WAL piles up on /data.

panels.title: Last restore test
panels.description: Result of the most recent automated test restore (monthly): restore the latest backup to scratch space, replay WAL, check every database.

panels.title: Restore test passed
panels.description: Time since a test restore last passed. They run monthly.

panels.title: Connections by state
panels.description: Client connections. idle_in_transaction: a session holding a transaction open while doing nothing, which blocks vacuum and can hold locks.

panels.title: Connections by user
panels.description: Client connections per database role. Roles with no connections are not shown.

panels.title: Transactions per second
panels.description: Committed plus rolled-back transactions.

panels.title: Rows per second
panels.description: Rows read (scanned or fetched by index) and rows inserted, updated or deleted, over the selected databases.

panels.title: Statements per second
panels.description: Statements executed (pg_stat_statements). The postgres database includes the monitoring endpoint's own queries, about 40 a minute.

panels.title: Mean statement time
panels.description: Average execution time per statement over each interval. Empty when nothing ran.

targets.expr: sum by (server, datname) (rate(pg_statements_exec_seconds_total{server=~"$server", datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (server, datname) (rate(pg_statements_calls_total{server=~"$server", datname=~"$datname"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Longest running statement, oldest transaction
panels.description: Age of the longest-running active statement and of the oldest open transaction, at each sample. A transaction left open for hours holds back vacuum.

panels.title: Waiting on locks, deadlocks
panels.description: Sessions blocked waiting for a lock at each sample, and deadlocks detected per interval.

panels.title: Database size
panels.description: Size on disk of each database (tables, indexes, TOAST). Updated every 5 minutes.

panels.title: Data disk used
panels.description: Space used on the /data partition (left axis; 'Data disk free' above has the share left), and how much of it is WAL in pg_wal (right axis), which grows if archiving to the backup repository falls behind.

panels.title: WAL written per hour
panels.description: Write-ahead log generated. All of it is archived to the backup repository, so this drives the repository's growth between full backups.

panels.title: Transaction ID age
panels.description: Age of each database's oldest unfrozen transaction ID. Autovacuum freezes at 200 million; PostgreSQL stops accepting writes near 2 billion. Steady growth past 200 million means vacuum can't keep up (often a long-open transaction).

panels.title: Backup size
panels.description: All retained backups in the pgBackRest repository on shire (compressed), next to the total size of the databases. Archived WAL, also kept in the repository, is not measured: that would mean walking the repository on NFS. Updated every 5 minutes.

panels.title: Size of the last backup
panels.description: What the most recent backup of each type added to the repository, compressed. Incrementals store only changed blocks.

panels.title: Backup duration
panels.description: How long the most recent backup of each type took.

panels.title: WAL archiving
panels.description: WAL segments copied to the backup repository per interval, and failed attempts (PostgreSQL retries failures). A few failures right after a new server's first start, before the backup repository exists, are expected.

panels.title: Replicas and slots
panels.description: Replicas streaming from this server, and its replication slots. An inactive slot keeps WAL on disk forever and can fill /data.

panels.title: Replication lag
panels.description: As a primary: the largest replay lag among its replicas. As a replica: time since the last transaction replayed from the primary (this also grows while the primary is idle).

panels.title: WAL held for replicas
panels.description: The most WAL any replication slot is keeping on disk, and how far behind the furthest replica is, in bytes.
